name: ASSAY OFFICE, FRONT
note:
POINTERS, NOT ANSWERS. Every entry here names where a canonical source lives; whether that source is COMPLETE is computed by tools/check-room-readiness.mjs, never asserted here. No line of the fiction appears in this file -- the words stay in /docs, and a readiness record that quoted them would be a second copy of the writing drifting from the first.

The declaration exists because 'which sections cover Room 5' cannot be derived: doc 02's puzzle table has no room column, doc 04's trees are per character, and doc 03's pairs are per duel. A tool guessing at that would answer confidently and wrongly. So the pointers are declared and auditable, and the completeness tests are mechanical.

examine.primaryNote: #1 and #2 are not a formatting quirk. Doc 05 names this room twice: once for its own examine layer and once, 1200 lines later, in the act-variant section. Both headings are correct, neither may be renamed to suit a tool, and an unqualified reference would silently read whichever came first.

staging.why: A staging/beat script is doc 17's opening and doc 43's Room 1 machinery -- a scripted sequence of timed beats. Room 5 has no scripted sequence in any canonical document: it is entered, examined and talked in. `check-gauntlet-script` and the sequence runner are not involved.
